(`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

country.comment: Empirical study conducted in Piyungan Subdistrict, Bantul Regency, Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia.

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative AHP priority weights and consistency/consensus metrics are reported alongside qualitative interview findings; no regression or causal treatment-effect estimate is estimated.
effect_estimate.value: In Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) pairwise comparisons across 8 rural water systems (RWS), social criteria ranked highest in sustaining RWS financing (45%), followed by economic (36%) and environmental criteria (19%; CR = 0.001702, consensus = 85.8%), with community-based management (25%), financial management (14%), community participation (12%), and willingness to pay (11%) as the top sub-criteria. Among four financing alternatives, community financing via user tariffs and connection fees ranked highest at 62% priority, followed by private financing (13.7% in text; 14% in Table 2), grant funding (12.5% in text; 13% in Table 2), and debt financing (11.4% in text; 11% in Table 2; CR = 0.00482, consensus = 81%). Qualitative stakeholder interviews documented that lack of formal legal status, consensus-based tariffs below full cost recovery, and weak financial governance block access to formal credit and contributed to several RWS ceasing operations when unable to fund pump and pipeline repairs.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 3-4, Section 3 Result and Discussion, Table 1, Figure 1, and Table 2
